newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mobil unit, Dubai firm in shipping venture.
newsitem.headline: Mobil unit, Dubai firm in shipping venture.

text.p: The Mobil Shipping and Transportation Company, a unit of the U.S. Mobil Corp, and Dubai Investments on Sunday announced they had formed a 50-50 shipping joint venture, primarily to transport crude for Mobil.

The partners said the venture, called the Dubai Mobil Shipping Company or DUMOCO, had already purchased a double-hull VLCC (Very Large Crude Carrier) for $85 million, financed in equal parts by equity and a December U.S bond issue.

"It is the first joint venture between Dubai Investments and Mobil. But I believe there are many to come," Anis al-Jallaf, chairman of Dubai Investments, told a news conference. Dubai Investments is a public joint stock company.

The ship, built by Japan's Sumitomo Corp, is the new company's only asset to date and was previously owned by Mobil. The joint venture provides that the 300,000-tonne Eagle, which can carry 2.2 million barrels of oil, will be leased back to Mobil, Mobil officials said.
"It is a special purpose company formed to buy the ship," one official said.
"The ship will be primarily employed in Mobil's business and will be run by Mobil," said Gerhard Kurz, president of the Mobil Shipping and Transportation Company.
DUMOCO, which is incorporated in the Cayman Islands, was founded on December 2, 1996. But the deal was only announced on Sunday to coincide with its first board meeting.
The joint venture will be run by current senior management of the Mobil Shipping and Transportation Company and Dubai Investments.
"We are interested in broadening our connection with Dubai," Kurz said. "We intend to be part of the growth of this centre of economic activity."

Dubai Investments, a Gulf investment company, was established in 1995 with a capital of $355 million and a United Arab Emirates investor base of 32,000 shareholders. -- Caroline Drees, Dubai newsroom +9714-6071-219
